text: Opt-in caller-owned compile cache landed: PlotCompileCache (core shared, public API). Two LRU levels — trained data keyed by (plot, options) reference identity, placements keyed by (trained identity, context observable value: dimensions/resolution field-wise, textMetrics+fontRegistry by reference). Explicit capacities (bounded(trained=8, placed=32), zero retains nothing, negatives clamp), PlotCacheProfile reports trainedHits/Misses, placedHits/Misses, evictions, entry counts, hitRate. Disabled is a case object routed straight to the uncached path — zero overhead, empty profile. Errors propagate uncached. Reachable from the public DSL: PlotProgram.resolve(context, cache) and PlotBuilder.resolve(context, cache) (stable plot reference across builds keeps identity keys honest — the JavaFxViewerHost trap noted in the issue is avoided by putting the cache parameter on the surface consumers already call). Receipt: resize-cached (5-size sweep, warm) 0.069 ms / 0.19 MB vs resize-place 4.3 ms / 1.1 MB vs resize-only 807 ms / 1.5 GB; phase clock records zero compile phases on warm hits. PlotCompileCacheSuite (9 tests, shared → runs JVM+JS): scene equality vs uncached, both-level hits return identical instance, per-context placement reuse, identity-miss semantics, LRU eviction with dependent-placement drop, zero capacity, error non-caching, Disabled contract, DSL reachability. TimingWorkloadSuite asserts cached sweep reproduces uncached checksum with expected hit/miss ledger. docs/limits.md 'no caching of compiled plots' claim replaced with the real contract; performance/README.md updated. coreJVM 484 + coreJS 478 + performanceJVM 10 green; docs/mdoc green. Tree remains shared/dirty; not committed.
